key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca3PX3 perovskites strongly tunes stability, bandgap, and solar-cell performance, with Ca3PI3 emerging as the best photovoltaic candidate.
engineering_relevance: This points to composition engineering as a practical route for optimizing perovskite absorbers for higher-efficiency solar devices.
method: First-principles structural analysis of Ca3PX3 (X = F, Cl, Br, I)
Electronic band-structure calculations to determine bandgap type and size
Optical screening using SLME to estimate photovoltaic efficiency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps of 2.0–3.788 eV and SLME results spanning from 0.6% for Ca3PF3 to 29.6% for Ca3PI3.
watch_item: The reported efficiencies are computational screening results, so experimental synthesis stability and device-level losses still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
